newsitem.title: USA: Study puts higher cost on Boston's 'Big Dig'.
newsitem.headline: Study puts higher cost on Boston's 'Big Dig'.

text.p: A study has found that the cost of the massive infrastructure project in downtown Boston commonly called the "Big Dig" has risen to just under $11 billion, the Boston Globe reported Wednesday.

Despite assurances by state transportation officials that the cost would not rise over $10.4 billion, expensive measures taken to limit the project's impact on city life has driven the price higher, according to the study.
The seven-month study of the Central Artery/Ted Williams Tunnel project was conducted by the John W. McCormack Institute of Public Affairs at the University of Massachusetts at Boston.
"The pressure on the budget is upward, in part as a result of measures required to control noise and dust and to maintain traffic flow in downtown Boston," the study concluded.
The study found the project's own internal documents show a current project completion cost estimate of $10.96 billion, the Globe said.
"Big Dig" project coordinator Peter Zuk told the Globe that the previous $10.4 billion estimate will be difficult to meet.
"We continue to work hard every day to contain the cost of this project and we are confident there are steps we can take to move us back to $10.4 billion," he said.
